questions.q: What are the three layers of a well-built dbt project, in build order?
options: Sources, staging, marts
Staging, sources, marts
Marts, staging, sources
Raw, warehouse, report
questions.explain: Sources are declared first (pointing at raw data), staging models clean that data 1:1, and marts build the final business logic on top.

questions.q: How many real dbt models does this Beginner capstone plan for, total?
options: Two — one staging model and one mart model
Ten, one per lesson
Five, one per data layer
One, a single model that does everything
questions.explain: The plan is deliberately the smallest real version of the pattern: one source, one staging model, and one mart model — two models total.

questions.q: Why can't the mart model (Lesson 8) be built before the staging model (Lesson 6) exists?
options: It can be built first — order doesn't matter in dbt
dbt requires all models to be written in a single file first
Snowflake requires models to be created in alphabetical order
The mart model references the staging model with ref(), which only resolves once that model exists
questions.explain: dbt models depend on each other through ref() and source() calls; the mart's ref('stg_jaffle_shop__customers') call only works once that staging model exists, which is why the project builds bottom-up.

questions.q: Why does this project's plan NOT include an intermediate layer between staging and marts?
options: Intermediate layers are only for SQL Server projects, not Snowflake
dbt doesn't support intermediate models
With only one source table, there's nothing to join yet, so an intermediate layer isn't needed
Intermediate models are never used in real dbt projects
questions.explain: An intermediate layer typically exists to join multiple tables before a final mart; with a single source table, there's nothing yet to join, so this minimal plan skips it.

questions.q: What is the main risk of skipping the planning step and just writing one big model that does everything at once?
options: It mixes raw-data cleanup with business logic in one file, making it painful to debug and impossible to reuse
dbt will refuse to run a project with only one model
Snowflake charges more for single-model projects
It guarantees the tests in Lesson 7 will fail
questions.explain: Skipping the layered plan is how beginners end up with one model trying to do everything — a classic debugging and reuse headache that the sources/staging/marts pattern is designed to avoid.
